steps.explain: Angles at \(O\) add to \(360^\circ\). \(\angle AOC=\angle DOF=90^\circ\) (square corners).
Write \(\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OF}\) with the angle formula, using \(\cos(180^\circ-\theta)=-\cos\theta\).
Sides of a square are equal: \(|2\mathbf a|=|2\mathbf c|\) and \(|2\mathbf f|=|2\mathbf d|\).
Divide both sides by 4.

parts.answer: ∠AOC = ∠DOF = 90°, so ∠AOF = 360° − 90° − 90° − θ = 180° − θ. Then \(2\mathbf a\cdot2\mathbf f=|2\mathbf a||2\mathbf f|\cos(180°-\theta)=-|2\mathbf a||2\mathbf f|\cos\theta\). As |2a| = |2c| and |2f| = |2d| (sides of squares), this equals \(-|2\mathbf c||2\mathbf d|\cos\theta=-2\mathbf c\cdot2\mathbf d\). Dividing by 4: \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf f=-\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf d\).

keyPoints.note: Find ∠AOF in terms of θ, then compare OA·OF with OC·OD.

steps.explain: Use (i).
By (iii), \(-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf f=\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf d\), which cancels \(-\mathbf d\cdot\mathbf c\).
\(OD\perp OF\) and \(OA\perp OC\) (square corners), so both dot products are 0.
So \(WY\perp WZ\). With \(|WY|=|WZ|\) from (ii), the parallelogram \(WYXZ\) has a pair of equal, perpendicular adjacent sides, so it is a square.

B compares with the length of \(\mathbf v\), which has nothing to do with the shadow. Counterexample: \(\mathbf u=2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j\), \(\mathbf v=\mathbf i\).
So B is not always correct.
